claims.text: Increasing Ru content relative to an equiatomic PtPdRhRuIrOs baseline enhances ethanol oxidation performance.
Increasing Ru content induces local electronic-structure modifications in the catalyst.
Increasing Ru content changes local lattice strain in the catalyst.
A higher Ru fraction shifts the d-band center of active surface atoms.
A higher Ru fraction alters surface strain.
The Ru-induced electronic and strain changes reduce the binding energy of key oxygenated intermediates.
Weaker adsorption of oxygenated intermediates reduces catalyst poisoning.
Reduced poisoning facilitates more efficient ethanol oxidation.
Ru-enriched catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current density than the equiatomic catalyst under identical conditions.
Ru enrichment will alter the ethanol-oxidation product distribution in a manner indicative of reduced over-oxidation.
Ru-enriched catalysts will have lower coverage of poisoning intermediates than the equiatomic baseline.
The proposed relationships apply while the nanoscale catalyst remains a solid solution without phase separation or significant morphological change.
The magnitude of the Ru-enrichment effect may depend on Ru content and reaction conditions.
Prior observations support the proposed link between Ru-induced electronic or strain changes and improved performance.
